name: Banh It towers
kicker: Four Cham towers on a hill
summary: Four Cham towers on a hill about 20 km out: walk the group in about 30 minutes, for 15,000 đồng. They date from the late 11th century into the early 12th, and from the road the silhouette reads as a bánh ít cake. The French record name is Tour d'Argent. Tháp Đôi is the pair inside the city.
getThere: About 20 km from the city, beside Highway 1.

notice.title: This stop is the hill group
notice.body: Tháp Đôi is the pair inside the city. These four towers stand on a hill about 20 km out, beside Highway 1.

body: The four towers stand on a hill between two branches of the Kon River, Tân An and Cầu Gành, beside National Highway 1. From a distance the outline is the bánh ít cake that gave the group its everyday name. The French record calls it Tour d'Argent, the Silver Tower. Each tower has its own plan. The Ministry of Culture and Information ranked the group an architecture-and-art relic in 1982.

The address line is thôn Đại Lễ, xã Tuy Phước Bắc. The description places the same hill in xã Phước Hiệp, Tuy Phước, about 20 km from the city. The ticket is 15,000 đồng. Hours run from 7:00 to 18:00, and the posted visit is 30 minutes. They date from the late 11th century into the early 12th.
